Title: Why a tax refund feels like free money
Hook: Same money. Why does a refund feel free?
Real-life scenario: Spending a refund on something you'd never buy from salary
Evidence anchors (verify at production): Thaler 1985, 1999 (mental accounting); Epley, Mak & Idson 2006 (rebate vs bonus framing, J Behav Decis Making)

Title: Why a raise stops feeling like a raise
Hook: The raise felt huge. Six months later, nothing.
Real-life scenario: Lifestyle quietly rising to meet a new salary
Evidence anchors (verify at production): Brickman, Coates & Janoff-Bulman 1978; Lyubomirsky 2011 hedonic adaptation review (Oxford Handbook of Stress, Health, and Coping); Housel 2020 as idea source only

Series: The decision you didn't notice making
Title: Why your quick task always takes longer
Hook: You said 20 minutes. It took two hours.
Mechanism / intersection: Planning fallacy + focus on best-case scenario
Evidence anchors (verify at production): Kahneman & Tversky 1979 (planning fallacy); Buehler, Griffin & Ross 1994 (JPSP)

Series: The decision you didn't notice making
Title: Why less information can make you more sure
Hook: You heard one side. You felt certain.
Mechanism / intersection: WYSIATI (what you see is all there is) + coherence-based confidence
Real-life scenario: Judging a coworker from one story
Visual concept: Puzzle with missing pieces looking complete
Evidence anchors (verify at production): Kahneman 2011 (as synthesis); Brenner, Koehler & Tversky 1996, On the evaluation of one-sided evidence (J Behav Decis Making)

Series: The invisible rules of human behavior
Title: Why how you react to good news matters so much
Hook: They shared good news. Your reply changed everything.
Real-life scenario: Partner shares a promotion; you say 'nice' and keep scrolling
Evidence anchors (verify at production): Gable, Reis, Impett & Asher 2004 (JPSP); Gable, Gonzaga & Strachman 2006 (JPSP)

Title: Why sliding into a big step differs from deciding
Hook: Moving in felt easy. Deciding never happened.
Mechanism / intersection: Sliding vs deciding + inertia in commitment
Real-life scenario: Moving in together because a lease ran out
Visual concept: Two paths: drift arrow vs decision fork
Evidence anchors (verify at production): Stanley, Rhoades & Markman 2006 (Family Relations); Rhoades, Stanley & Markman 2009, pre-engagement cohabitation effect (J Family Psychology). Correlational: say 'linked to'
